title: Melting point as a test of purity
caption: A pure compound melts sharply, over a degree or so, at its known melting point: benzoic acid at 122 °C. Impurities disrupt the lattice, so an impure sample melts lower and over a wider range.
alt: Temperature scale with two bars: pure benzoic acid melting from 121.5 to 122.5 °C, and an impure sample melting from 114 to 119 °C.

checks.name: the impure sample finishes melting below the pure one starts
the impure range (5 °C) is wider than the pure one (1 °C)
